## Methods that I will implement:
**4) Tiered boarding**
First class boards in their section, business class boards in their section, economy boards in their section

**5) Completely random, but the passengers enter in waves**
For example, Southwest's open seating system (I don't think they do this anymore) with Groups A, B, and C

**6) Steffen Method**
Supposed to be the most optimal method

## Planning:
**4) Tiered Boarding**
72 passengers board a plane with 12 rows and 6 columns. There's one aisle down the middle of the plane. The 72 passengers are split into three groups: first class, business class, and economy. First class passengers board their section (rows 1 and 2). Business class passengers board their section (rows 3-5). Economy passengers board their section (rows 6-12). There are no assigned seats. The constraints are just that the groups enter in order, and each person in each group sits in a random, unoccupied seat of their section.

**5) Completely random, but the passengers enter in waves**
The 72 passengers are randomly split into three groups of 24 called A, B, and C. Group A passengers board first, and each Group A passenger takes a random, unoccupied seat anywhere in the plane. Groups B and C follow, but each subsequent group has fewer seats to choose from.

**6) Steffen Method**
The 72 passengers are lined up and seated in the following order, from back to front:
1) Window seat, odd-numbered
2) Window seat, even-numbered
3) Middle seat, odd-numbered
4) Middle seat, even-numbered
5) Aisle seat, odd-numbered
6) Aisle seat, even-numbered
It is supposed to be the most optimal boarding method.

## Coding
**5) Completely random, but the passengers enter in waves**

### Setting up
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
set.seed(67)

n_row <- 12
n_col <- 6
n_groups <- 3
n_passengers <- n_row * n_col

plane_mat <- matrix(0, nrow = n_row, ncol = n_col, byrow = TRUE)
print(plane_mat)   # The plane at the start of the simulation

target_seats <- 1:n_passengers

# Each passenger has an assigned group and a seat that they will randomly choose. Let's say that 87% of passengers use the overhead bin.
passengers <- data.frame(
  id = sample(target_seats), 
  group = sample(rep(1:n_groups, length.out = n_passengers)), 
  target_seat = target_seats, 
  target_row = c(rep(1:n_row, n_col)), 
  overhead = rbinom(n = n_passengers, size = 1, prob = 0.87)
)
passengers$overhead_time <- ifelse(passengers$overhead == 1, floor(rnorm(n = n_passengers, mean = 2.5, sd = 0.5)), 0)
passengers <- passengers %>%
  mutate(
    plane_mat_column = case_when(
      target_seat >= 1 & target_seat <= 12 ~ 1, 
      target_seat > 12 & target_seat <= 24 ~ 2, 
      target_seat > 24 & target_seat <= 36 ~ 3, 
      target_seat > 36 & target_seat <= 48 ~ 4, 
      target_seat > 48 & target_seat <= 60 ~ 5, 
      target_seat > 60 & target_seat <= 72 ~ 6
    ), 
    seat_type = case_when(
      plane_mat_column == 1 | plane_mat_column == 6 ~ "window", 
      plane_mat_column == 2 | plane_mat_column == 5 ~ "middle", 
      plane_mat_column == 3 | plane_mat_column == 4 ~ "aisle"
    )
  )

target_mat <- plane_mat + passengers$id
print(target_mat)   # The positions of all the passengers after they have boarded

# Determine the order in which the passengers enter the plane

# Group A
group_a <- passengers %>% filter(group == 1)
shuffled_idx_a <- sample(nrow(group_a))
group_a_order <- data.frame(
  id = group_a$id[shuffled_idx_a], 
  target_row = group_a$target_row[shuffled_idx_a], 
  overhead_time = group_a$overhead_time[shuffled_idx_a], 
  plane_mat_column = group_a$plane_mat_column[shuffled_idx_a]
)

# Group B
group_b <- passengers %>% filter(group == 2)
shuffled_idx_b <- sample(nrow(group_b))
group_b_order <- data.frame(
  id = group_b$id[shuffled_idx_b], 
  target_row = group_b$target_row[shuffled_idx_b], 
  overhead_time = group_b$overhead_time[shuffled_idx_b], 
  plane_mat_column = group_b$plane_mat_column[shuffled_idx_b]
)

# Group C
group_c <- passengers %>% filter(group == 3)
shuffled_idx_c <- sample(nrow(group_c))
group_c_order <- data.frame(
  id = group_c$id[shuffled_idx_c], 
  target_row = group_c$target_row[shuffled_idx_c], 
  overhead_time = group_c$overhead_time[shuffled_idx_c], 
  plane_mat_column = group_c$plane_mat_column[shuffled_idx_c]
)

```

### The Simulation Function
```{r}

# Function for boarding a group
board_group <- function(group_order_df, plane_mat, time) {

  # Initialize things
  next_person <- 1
  aisle_df <- data.frame(
    in_aisle = rep(0, length.out = n_row), 
    row_num = 1:n_row
  )
  
  while (next_person <= nrow(group_order_df) || any(aisle_df$in_aisle > 0)) {
    time <- time + 1
  
    for (i in seq_len(n_row)) {     # Loop through the rows of the plane
      if (aisle_df$in_aisle[i] > 0) {     # If there is a person in the aisle
        target <- group_order_df$target_row[group_order_df$id == aisle_df$in_aisle[i]]     # Get that person's target row
      
        if (i == target) {     # If that person is in their target row
          # Handling the overhead bins
          overhead_time <- group_order_df$overhead_time[group_order_df$id == aisle_df$in_aisle[i]]     # Get that person's overhead time
          time <- time + overhead_time     # Add their overhead time to the overall time
        
          # Updating that person's location
          plane_mat[i, group_order_df$plane_mat_column[group_order_df$id == aisle_df$in_aisle[i]]] <- aisle_df$in_aisle[i]     # Add them to the plane matrix
          aisle_df$in_aisle[i] <- 0     # Remove that person from the aisle
        }
      }
    }
    aisle_df$in_aisle <- c(0, aisle_df$in_aisle[-n_row])     # Move everyone in the queue forward by one position
  
    if (next_person <= nrow(group_order_df)) {     # If there is still someone yet to enter the plane aisle
      aisle_df$in_aisle[1] <- group_order_df$id[next_person]     # Assign them to the first position of the aisle, which is now empty
      next_person <- next_person + 1
    }
  
    # print(aisle_df$in_aisle)
  
  }

return(list(plane_mat, time))

}

```

### Getting the Results
```{r}
# Group A
plane_mat_pre_a <- matrix(0, nrow = n_row, ncol = n_col, byrow = TRUE)
time_pre_a <- 0

print("Before A")
print(plane_mat_pre_a)
print(time_pre_a)

board_group_a_results <- board_group(group_a_order, plane_mat_pre_a, time_pre_a)

# Group B
plane_mat_pre_b <- board_group_a_results[[1]]
time_pre_b <- board_group_a_results[[2]]

print("Before B")
print(plane_mat_pre_b)
print(time_pre_b)

board_group_b_results <- board_group(group_b_order, plane_mat_pre_b, time_pre_b)

# Group C
plane_mat_pre_c <- board_group_b_results[[1]]
time_pre_c <- board_group_b_results[[2]]

print("Before C")
print(plane_mat_pre_c)
print(time_pre_c)

board_group_c_results <- board_group(group_c_order, plane_mat_pre_c, time_pre_c)

# Final
plane_mat_final <- board_group_c_results[[1]]
time_final <- board_group_c_results[[2]]

print("Final")
print(plane_mat_final)
print(time_final)
```

#### Things to Add:
- Passengers actually getting to their seats once they're out of the aisle

"Person" is someone who just reached their target row and put their luggage in the overhead bin (if applicable):
If their seat is the aisle seat:
  They sit down immediately.
If their seat is the middle seat:
  If there is no one in the aisle seat, they proceed to their seat.
  If there is someone in the aisle seat, the person in the aisle seat gets up, lets the person sit down in the middle seat, and goes back to their seat.
If their seat is the window seat:
  If there is no one in the aisle or middle seats, they proceed to their seat.
  If there is someone in both the aisle and middle seats, both get up to let the person through, and then they go back to their seats.
  If there is one person in either the aisle or middle seats, they get up, let the person sit down in the window seat, and goes back to their seat.
